subject: Scoped log hold request & DPA addendum for BrightHealth investigation
messages:
From: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@brighthealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@brighthealth.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: scoped log hold + DPA addendum for BrightHealth investigation

Hi Sean,

Apologies for the short notice. Our legal team has opened an internal investigation and we need Redwood's help to preserve logs and backups for a narrowly scoped set of customer IDs (we'll provide the ID list later today). Specifically: 

- We need an extension of log retention for 180 days for the specified IDs beyond your standard 30-day TTL.
- We need a backup snapshot retained off-cycle for the date range 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-31 and a certified deletion-proof manifest when the hold is lifted.
- Please share an updated DPA addendum or amendment that covers temporary scoped holds and any cost estimate for the extended retention.
- We also need the current subprocessor list and confirmation if any subprocessors move data outside the EU for the affected accounts (BrightHealth has EU subsidiaries involved).

I attached a short spreadsheet with the investigation scope and a high-level timeline. Can you confirm feasibility and next steps by EOD PST?

Thanks,
Emily Barnes
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
BrightHealth

Attachments: BrightHealth_hold_packet.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: scoped log hold + DPA addendum for BrightHealth investigation

Emily — thanks for the details and the file. We can support a scoped temporary hold but need to confirm a few things to scope the work and get Legal/CS/Infra aligned: 

1) Final list of customer IDs (or dataset identifiers) and whether the hold is required for logs only or for backups/snapshots + logs.
2) Exact retention window: you asked for +180 days beyond the 30-day TTL — do you want a hard 180-day extension from the original event date or a rolling 180 days from when the hold is applied?
3) Whether BrightHealth requires additional audit or notarized deletion manifests when the hold is lifted (we can produce certificates but need lead time).
4) Are EU subsidiaries the owner of the account data or are they acting as controllers that require additional DPA clauses for cross-border transfers? That will affect subprocessor disclosures and transfer mechanisms.

Kimberly — looping you in to draft an addendum and confirm any legal gating items. Marissa — can you estimate ops/infra time and a rough cost delta for 180-day scoped retention + snapshot escrow? Karthik — heads up for sales/contracting so we can route DocuSign if needed.

We can turn around a proposed addendum and subprocessor list by tomorrow EOD PT if Legal is comfortable with the scoped language.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: scoped log hold + DPA addendum for BrightHealth investigation

Thanks Sean — draft language and operational constraints below. I attached two artifacts: a proposed DPA addendum (DPA_scoped-hold-addendum_v1.pdf) and our current subprocessor disclosure (subprocessor_disclosure_v2.csv).

Summary (legal view):
- Scope: Temporary "scoped hold" limited to the list of IDs provided by BrightHealth. Hold applies to logs and backups/snapshots explicitly called out.
- Duration model: We propose a two-tier model to balance operational cost and legal certainty: 
  * Tier A (preferred): Rolling hold — extend retention for affected IDs to 180 days from the time the hold is applied.
  * Tier B (alternative): Fixed hold — retain specified snapshots until the stated investigation closure date, with a mandatory review at 180 days.
- Escrow/fallback: If Redwood is contractually required to maintain an immutable copy offsite for evidentiary purposes, we will escrow the snapshot in a WORM-enabled storage and provide a signed integrity manifest. Additional escrow costs will apply.
- Data transfers/subprocessors: Our current disclosure lists subprocessors and their regions. For any subprocessor that routes data outside the EU, Redwood can:
  * provide SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses) where applicable, and
  * on request, provide a redacted copy of processor locations and subprocessors that handled the affected IDs.
- Audit trail & proof of deletion: On release we can provide an audit log + signed deletion manifest. Proof-of-deletion for offsite escrow will require coordination with the escrow provider (additional lead time).

Operational asks from Marissa: we need the exact ID list; if the list is > 10k IDs or spans multiple tenants/regions, ops may require a 48–72 hour lead time to schedule snapshot and to ensure no conflicting retention jobs run. Cost: preliminary estimate for 180-day keep + escrow is $7k–$18k depending on snapshot size and WORM storage duration — ops will provide a granular estimate after ID list + snapshot size.

Next steps proposed: 
1) Emily provides ID list and confirms Tier A vs Tier B.
2) Redwood returns redlined DPA addendum and subprocessor list (attached).
3) Execution via DocuSign and operations kickoff with a scoped M.A.P. (mutual action plan) including rollback/restore runbook.

I recommend we keep the DPA addendum intentionally narrow — limited to this investigation and explicitly time-boxed. If BrightHealth anticipates repeated holds we should negotiate a standing addendum.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_scoped-hold-addendum_v1.pdf, subprocessor_disclosure_v2.csv

From: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@brighthealth.com>

Cc: finance@brighthealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: scoped log hold + DPA addendum for BrightHealth investigation

Kimberly / Sean — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear options. BrightHealth prefers Tier A (rolling 180-day extension from hold application) and we confirm the hold will be for both logs and the backup snapshot covering 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-31.

A few action items from our side: 
- We'll send the CSV of IDs by EOD PST today.
- Please route the DPA addendum through DocuSign (finance will need to approve cost). Could you include a short cost breakdown (ops estimate + escrow delta) so our finance team can pre-approve?
- Regarding subprocessors: our EU subsidiaries require a redacted subprocessor list and SCC confirmation. If you can flag any subprocessors that perform processing in the EU vs non-EU that would be ideal.

If you can get a DocuSign packet and cost estimate by tomorrow lunchtime ET, we can aim to sign and kick off ops by Thursday.

Thanks,
Emily
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
BrightHealth
